issues.title: PartialGroupInfo: say how the signed GroupInfo is rebuilt
issues.author: MarkAtwood
issues.body:
§4 says the hub can recreate most of the GroupInfo from the handshake messages, but leaves the details implicit, and the joiner has to rebuild exactly the bytes the committer signed. Three things would pin it down:

1. A normative pointer: the GroupInfo is rebuilt per RFC 9420 §12.4.3, from the post-commit GroupContext and the Commit's confirmation_tag.
2. Where `ratchet_tree` goes in the rebuilt extension list. The signature covers the list in order, and implementations already differ for ordinary GroupInfos: OpenMLS puts ratchet_tree first, mls-rs appends it.
3. What a receiver does if `group_info_extensions` contains a ratchet_tree anyway. The text only says the sender omits it. Suggest MUST reject.

Found implementing -01 in mimid, which puts ratchet_tree first and rejects one that's present.

comments.author: rohanmahy
comments.body:
The signature has to be over the extensions that were actually present. If whichever client created the GroupInfo did not include the `ratchet_tree` extension, then it won't appear in the signature, so the signature will depend on the choices in `RatchetTreePresence`.

I would recommend that the GroupInfo.extensions appear in ascending numerical order of the extension IDs. We have that for Components, but not for extensions. It is a bit of a backwards compatibility issue.

comments.author: MarkAtwood
comments.body:
Ascending order works for me. On back compat, could we scope the rule to the GroupInfo rebuilt from a PartialGroupInfo? That's new in this draft, so nothing existing has to change, and the committer just has to sign in that order when it intends the hub to send a partial one.

Still worth a line for the other two: point at 9420 §12.4.3 for the rebuild, and say what a receiver does if group_info_extensions has a ratchet_tree in it anyway (I'd reject).

comments.author: rohanmahy
comments.body: As I thought about implementation efficiency, I think having the `ratchet_tree` extension be last in the GroupInfo.extensions actually makes the most sense.

issues.title: §4: "ratchet_tree MUST be last" has to bind every committer; OpenMLS and mls-rs (GREASE) don't put it last
issues.author: MarkAtwood
issues.body:
-02 §4 says: "For implementations that support PartialGroupInfo, if the ratchet_tree extension is ever present in the signed GroupInfo, it MUST be the last element in the extension list."

The scope doesn't work. The committer signs the GroupInfo, but whether it later travels as a PartialGroupInfo is decided afterwards, by a hub or DS the committer may know nothing about. A receiver that rebuilds the full GroupInfo by appending ratchet_tree can verify the signature only if the committer put ratchet_tree last. So the rule has to bind every committer that includes ratchet_tree, whether or not it supports PartialGroupInfo, and RFC 9420 puts no order on GroupInfo extensions.

Current implementations don't put it last:

- OpenMLS (main, `commit_builder.rs`) adds ratchet_tree first, then the application's GroupInfo extensions, then external_pub. Any GroupInfo with ratchet_tree and external_pub has ratchet_tree first.
- mls-rs puts ratchet_tree after external_pub, but with its `grease` feature it adds a GREASE extension at the end just before signing.

A GroupInfo signed by either can't be sent as a PartialGroupInfo that verifies after reconstruction.

Either of these fixes it:

1. Require it of every committer: a GroupInfo that contains ratchet_tree MUST have it as the last extension, GREASE included. This needs existing implementations to change and a statement that it updates RFC 9420 behavior.
2. Carry the position: add the index ratchet_tree had in the signed extension list to PartialGroupInfo, and reinsert it there when rebuilding. This works with GroupInfos that existing implementations already sign.

Found implementing PartialGroupInfo reconstruction in mimid.

issues.title: §6.1 registers mls_partial_group_info but no MLSMessage arm uses it
issues.author: MarkAtwood
issues.body:
§6.1 (md L231-238) registers a wire format, `mls_partial_group_info` (0x0010 suggested), but the body never uses it. Nothing adds a `case mls_partial_group_info: PartialGroupInfo partial_group_info;` arm to the RFC 9420 §6 `MLSMessage` `select (wire_format)`, nothing says when a PartialGroupInfo is sent MLSMessage-framed and when it travels bare next to a commit, and nothing says whether a member must list the new value in `supported_wire_formats` / `required_wire_formats` (draft-ietf-mls-extensions).

As written, one implementation can send a framed `MLSMessage{wire_format=0x0010}` while another sends bare `PartialGroupInfo` bytes, and a receiver can't tell which it got. A codepoint with no defined encoding also can't be checked against capabilities.

Suggested fix: add the `MLSMessage` arm, state where PartialGroupInfo is MLSMessage-framed and where (if anywhere) it is carried bare, and say whether `mls_partial_group_info` must appear in `supported_wire_formats` before a committer sends one. If it is never framed, drop the registration.

issues.title: §4: PartialGroupInfo ratchet_tree rejection has no keyword and no scope
issues.author: MarkAtwood
issues.body:
§4 (md L191-197): "If a PartialGroupInfo is received with a `ratchet_tree` extension, the entire message is rejected."

There is no BCP 14 keyword, so this isn't a requirement on the receiver, and "the entire message" is undefined: the PartialGroupInfo alone, or the commit bundle / MIMI update that carries it. Rejecting the PartialGroupInfo but processing the commit leaves the hub unable to rebuild the GroupInfo; rejecting the whole bundle drops a valid commit. Two hubs that pick differently diverge on the same input.

Suggested fix: "A receiver MUST reject a PartialGroupInfo whose `group_info_extensions` contains a `ratchet_tree` extension", and state what happens to the commit it accompanies, or defer that to the carrying protocol.

issues.title: 0x000A is still read as last_resort by OpenMLS
issues.author: MarkAtwood
issues.body:
§6.2 suggests 0x000A for ratchet_tree_source_domains. mls-extensions-04 and -05 suggested the same value for the last_resort_key_package extension, and OpenMLS still parses 0x000a that way. It expects an empty body, so a non-empty ratchet_tree_source_domains fails to decode instead of being skipped as unknown. That's true of 0.9.2 and of current main.

0x000A isn't registered, so the suggestion is fine on paper, and I filed the OpenMLS side as openmls/openmls#2318. But clients already deployed won't get that fix. Picking another value avoids the problem. Your coordination list has extension types up to 0x0011 taken, so 0x0012 looks free.

pulls.title: Fix ratchet_tree type, httpsUrl typo and external_pub description
pulls.author: MarkAtwood
pulls.body:
Three fixes from implementing -01 in mimid:

- `case full:` declares `Node ratchet_tree<V>`, but the ratchet_tree extension in RFC 9420 §12.4.3.3 is `optional<Node> ratchet_tree<V>`. A bare Node can't represent blank nodes, so most real trees can't be sent this way. Changed to `optional<Node>`. This changes the encoding, so happy to move it to an issue if you'd rather track it there.
- The enum value is `httpsUri` but the select arm says `case httpsUrl:`.
- `external_pub` is described as "the public key of the external commiter". In RFC 9420 it's the group's HPKE public key that external joiners encrypt to, not the joiner's. (Also "commiter".)

comments.body: I see. Each item in the Vec is an optional<Node>.  Wow, we could have saved an extraneous byte and an extra layer of encoding if we had just made NodeType 0 = `blank`.
I think I would rather change the enum definition to `httpsUrl`

```suggestion
the group's public key for external joiners whose private key is held by the
entire group. The `group_info_extensions` is often an empty list.
```

```suggestion
- `httpsUrl` indicates that the `ratchet_tree` can be downloaded from a
URL using the `https:` scheme.
```
